questions.q: Why does this report use Import mode instead of DirectQuery?
options: DirectQuery is not supported for SQL Server connections
The dataset is tiny and only needs to be pulled up during a meeting, not updated in real time
Import mode is required whenever a native query is used
DirectQuery cannot run queries that use GROUP BY
questions.explain: With at most four rows and no need for real-time updates, Import gives faster visuals and lets the file be built without the server needing to be reachable every time it's opened.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect Power BI to the data, rather than importing the raw tables directly?
options: By exporting the query results to a CSV file first and importing that
By pasting the full Lesson 3 T-SQL query into the SQL statement box under Get Data -> SQL Server -> Advanced options, as a native query
By manually recreating the five-table join inside Power Query's user interface
By using DirectQuery and relying on Power BI's automatic relationship detection
questions.explain: The Lesson 3 query is pasted into the native query box, so the join/filter/aggregation work happens on the SQL Server, not inside Power Query.

questions.q: What row count should this query's result never exceed when loaded into Power Query?
options: Ten rows
Four rows, since AdventureWorks2012 has exactly four product categories
There is no expected upper bound on row count
One row per sales territory
questions.explain: Because the data is grouped by category and there are only four categories in AdventureWorks2012, more than four rows would indicate a problem with the joins or grouping.

questions.q: What data type should TotalSalesAmount be confirmed as in Power Query?
options: True/False
Date/Time
Text
Decimal Number or Fixed Decimal Number
questions.explain: SQL Server's money/numeric types sometimes import as text if the connector guesses wrong, so confirming a Decimal or Fixed Decimal type here avoids DAX measures silently failing later.

questions.q: Why is the query renamed from the generic default to CategoryPerformanceSnapshot?
options: That name appears in the Power BI data model and should describe what the data actually holds
Power BI requires query names to match the SQL table name
Renaming is required before a native query can run
It changes which columns are included in the result
questions.explain: A descriptive query name matters because it's what shows up in the Fields pane and data model going forward -- "Query1" doesn't tell anyone what the data is.
